supported_claims.text: 睡 is analyzed as a phonosemantic compound: 目 contributes the eye-related meaning and 垂 supplies the sound cue. The Shuowen gloss is “sleep while sitting”; broader attested uses include sleeping and, in a later example, “lie down.”

The sound analysis has a same-system historical comparison: Baxter–Sagart gives 垂 *[d]o[j] and 睡 *[d]o[j]-s, with 睡 carrying an added *-s suffix. Their modern Mandarin readings are chuí and shuì, respectively.

The supplied curated glyph selection is empty. The available account identifies the Shuowen analysis but provides no verified image of 睡’s seal form or earlier physical inscription with which to trace graphic development.

disagreements.text: The Shuowen gloss and later commentary support an eye-related semantic analysis and a sound component, though the transmitted account is not independent proof of the graph’s earliest construction. A modern source also identifies 目 as semantic and 垂 as phonetic; these repeated analyses do not constitute independent corroboration.

limitations.text: The dossier does not establish 睡’s earliest physical attestation or detailed graphic evolution. The Shuowen gloss and examples in transmitted texts do not date surviving manuscripts or establish a chronological progression from sitting doze to sleep to lying down.

The sound comparison supports the phonetic analysis, but reconstruction similarity alone does not prove the historical relationship. The Unicode character pages were inaccessible; local reading rows supply the Mandarin pair but were not independently verified against those pages.

No evidence in this dossier supports treating 睡 as a whole-graph phonetic loan or as a graph corrupted from another form. Variant or error reports concern forms of 垂 and do not establish corruption in 睡.
